claim: Gyeongbokgung Palace adult admission is 3,000 won; free for those wearing hanbok, under-6, and seniors 65+, and free for everyone on Culture Day (last Wednesday monthly).
quote: Adult tickets cost 3000 won, with 1500 won for children. Children six and younger, seniors 65+, and anyone wearing hanbok get in for free, and admission is free for everyone on Culture Day.

claim: Gyeongbokgung is open 09:00 with seasonal closing (17:00 Nov-Feb, 18:00 Mar-May & Sep-Oct, 18:30 Jun-Aug), closed Tuesdays.
quote: November-February 09:00-17:00, March-May & September-October 09:00-18:00, and June-August 09:00-18:30. The palace is closed on Tuesdays.

claim: Gyeongbokgung's royal changing-of-the-guard ceremony runs at 10:00 and 14:00 daily except Tuesdays, lasting about 20 minutes at Gwanghwamun Gate.
quote: The changing of the guard takes place at 10am and 2pm every day except Tuesdays... continues for about 20 minutes. The ceremony is held at Gwanghwamun Gate.

claim: Changdeokgung's Secret Garden (Huwon) requires an advance-booked guided tour costing 8,000 won for adults (combined with the 3,000-won palace entry), as daily visitor numbers are capped.
quote: adults (ages 19-64) cost 8,000 won... The main palace itself costs 3,000 won... entry is only permitted with a guided tour, so you must book a guided tour ticket in advance.

claim: Changdeokgung opens 09:00-17:00 (last entry 16:30, extended to 18:00 in summer) and is closed Mondays; the Secret Garden tour is a mandatory ~90-minute walk booked via royal.khs.go.kr.
quote: Changdeokgung operates from 9 AM to 5 PM... extended hours until 6 PM in summer months. The palace is closed on Mondays... The Secret Garden tour consists of a mandatory 90-minute tour.

claim: N Seoul Tower observatory admission is 29,000 won for adults and 23,000 won for children/seniors (official 2026 rate).
N Seoul Tower is open 10:00-23:00, with the observation deck closing to new visitors 30 minutes before closing.
quote: N Seoul Tower is open from 10:00-23:00. However, the observation deck is closed to new visitors 30 minutes prior to closing.

claim: The Namsan cable car to N Seoul Tower runs 10:00-23:00, takes about 3 minutes, and costs 15,000 won round-trip for adults (11,500 won children).
quote: Adult return tickets are priced at 15,000 won, while children's return tickets are 11,500 won. The Namsan Cable Car takes approximately three minutes to reach the summit.

claim: Gwangjang Market (Seoul's oldest market) is open daily ~08:30-18:00 with food stalls running later, famous for bindaetteok (mung-bean pancake), mayak kimbap, soondae, and hand-cut kalguksu noodles.
quote: famous for authentic street foods such as soondae (pork blood sausage), bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and hand-cut noodles

claim: Gwangjang Market's lunchtime rush (12:00-14:00) brings long queues; restaurants stay open until 23:00 and Sundays are quieter.
quote: Gwangjang Market is open daily between 8:30 am - 6 pm, though restaurants operate until 11:00pm... The lunchtime rush between 12 pm and 2 pm sees throngs of office workers.

claim: Namdaemun Market, one of Seoul's largest traditional markets, runs roughly 10:00 to 05:00 next-day with some wholesale shops open overnight, known for kalguksu and braised galchi (hairtail).
quote: Namdaemun Market is usually open from 10:00 AM to 5:00 AM the next day, making it one of the few places in Seoul that truly never sleeps.

claim: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Zaha Hadid's landmark neofuturist building, has free-to-access exterior, plazas and design store; open Tue-Sun 10:00-19:00 and closed Mondays (paid exhibitions vary).
quote: The exterior, Oulim Square, the Dongdaemun History & Culture Park, and the DDP Design Store are all free to access at any time.

claim: Bukchon Hanok Village's residential alleys (notably Bukchon-ro 11-gil) are a managed quiet zone restricting tourist entry before 10:00 and after 17:00, with a 100,000-won fine for violations.
quote: Access to the main residential alleys is strictly prohibited before 10:00 AM and after 05:00 PM... A fine of 100,000 won will be imposed on those who enter the area outside these hours for tourism purposes.
